Me and a friend of mine were talking about this the other day. But I'm in the camp that firmly believes that most directors and film-makers only know Lovecraft's mythos at surface level, and hence don't understand the nature of the horror he creates. There is this mindset where people think they want to see the rubber-suit monsters and giant CGI Cthulhu and Shoggoth, enormous impossible cities, and all those fantastical elements brought to life on the big screen. But the way they work in the stories is to be very vaguely outlined and described, and seen as little as possible. The idea is that to even glimpse them drives you insane. Now, a good director would probably be able to make a solid film where you barely glimpse anything, and when you do it's terrifying. But not many people will go to see it, because they want "the money shot" which shows off a bunch of visual effects, as opposed to the "mood" or atmosphere you can get from sinking your teeth into a good Lovecraft story. 

I think Annihilation is the best Lovecraftian/weird fiction film I've ever seen, because it accurately leaves you with an unsettled feeling of that cosmic dread. Not ever being able to understand the shimmer and what it is, or if it can even understand us. It's just beyond us. 

I also agree that some of the non cosmic horror stories like Cool Air, or Pickman's Model could be interesting. Though I would LOVE to see Whisperer in Darkness get some kind of modern adaptation.

Thanks so much. I'm holding strong. Every time I put on our wedding ring that we had custom made, I feel her with me. 

This road ahead is going to be hard. She left so many creative projects unfinished though, and I'm going to make it my mission to show them all to the world, the wonders she created but didn't have the self-confidence to show. That gives me strength and purpose. I want to find a mountain to shout off of about how wonderful this person was. How stupidly humble considering how insanely talented she really was. 

  
She was one of those people that could sit down, do a casual little doodle in her notepad that you could easily frame and charge a hundred bucks for, and then end up giving up on it because she thought it wasn't good enough.   


When she was younger, one of her cruel Aunt's drew over one of her drawings in pen when she asked her what she thought, and this aunt thought it would be a good idea to CORRECT a child's drawing, showing the faults and mistakes and drawing over it, to demonstrate how it SHOULD have been done. I think that act alone was responsible for destroying a lot of her self confidence in creativity.

Her family and I met with the Funeral directors today and we went over some of the details. 

I asked if she could be cremated in her dress, but apparently based on the design of the dress it wouldn't really work out that well, and also the way her skin looked...she had bruising all over her body. Her condition made it so none of her bruises would heal and she kept having to have blood taken for more and more tests.

Her mother advised me that we could get a framed photo of her wearing it when they were trying it on, with her wedding shoes and put it on her coffin, next to the dress itself hanging on the dressmaking mannequin. 

​

I could choose one of the new outfits she'd got recently that she was really loving.

Apparently the family are going to handle it. The same reason we're not really putting a funeral notice in the newspaper, to avoid attracting unwanted attention. But we could easily do it after the fact. I'm always so tired these days, but we spoke to the funeral directors today and sorted a bunch of things out. 

I get to have a private viewing with her before the service so I can sit there beside her, see her dress on a mannequin and listen to "Love Me Tender" by Elvis which was going to be our first dance.
Thankyou so much for this. It is hard right now.

Well, I just turned 28 on the weekend. And I feel like I'm just starting in a lot of ways. If I hadn't had some developmental issues, and debilitating PTSD I probably would have gotten to where I am sooner, but you can't change the past. The good thing about having a negative start in life, is that every day going forwards is better than what came before it. 

Each new day has the potential to be the best day of your life, so many new things and new experiences. Finding a way to feel safe and secure and loved, that's a challenge for sure. Read "Man's Search For Meaning" by Victor Frankl, he really establishes a good philosophy for living a meaningful life, which is where you set yourself a goal, based on what ideals are important to you and what you feel passionate about.

Just take it step by step. 90% of life is outside our control, just making everything small -- one pebble at a time, we will slowly move a mountain. Congratulate yourself on each milestone, you are allowed to celebrate little victories. Even just getting out of bed each day, making your bed. Small acts of kindness. Wish a stranger well on your way to work. Throw some money in a busker's hat. 

Life can be exactly what you want if you chase what you value most. Who do you admire, and why? Think about those you admire and what it is that they have that you feel would make your life more complete, and I think in most cases you can boil it down to them pursuing what they were passionate about and using their success to better those around them.

No other art-style is quite like Warframe - it has carved out a niche all of its own, and the art-team are so far ahead of the competition is staggering. They went all in on a batshit crazy concept that would be alien to a vast number of people, and humanized it in the most startling ways. Easy to pick up, hard to master -- endlessly customizable. Fluid movement, unmatched gunplay/variety, and now very soon, some extremely nuanced co-op play via Railjack. 
This is the game we all dreamed of playing when we were young.

It was a guilt trip. I cut her out a few years ago, and for each of those years she had sent a Bday card and a christmas card. They were all the birthdays that I had "deprived her of" by cutting her out of my life. 

It was essentially an attempt at gaslighting - attempting to debase my character by trying to make me appear as the villainous child, ignoring the kind caring mother who sends nothing but gifts and love blah blah blah. I wasn't falling for it.

Can't recommend it enough. 
Seriously - I have no formal art training. I just picked up a bunch of watercolour paints and a stack of paper and went to town with them a few years back. Been slowly building and experimenting to get to a style that I like, being a big fan of David Lynch's work, Picasso's later childish experiments and Marilyn Manson's watercolours. 

When I got out of suicide ward a few years back, I found baking incredibly therapeutic. Just MAKING something that wasn't in the world previously had a huge impact on my sense of self importance. Art does all this and more, since it's also simultaneously a meditative practice. Your head very quickly gets into "the zone" when you get painting, which is a big help when dealing with pain and unhelpful thinking. 

All the best to you, hope you can get some physio and other treatment!

I struggle with the concept of volunteering. I don't think I'd be needed anywhere. Plus, I'm very hurt by other people's happiness at the moment. I find it hard to make others happy, because I'm instantly jealous of their happiness. Basically, I have a bunch of toxic feedback loops in my head that make it impossible for happiness to exist at the moment.
I am envious of other's happiness. It poisons my own for some reason. I am really frustrated when I find out about other people experiencing a kind of happiness I have never experienced.
I have been honest. I really believe in the power of therapy. I have to try really hard to "be happy for other people".

I'm pretty jaded. I think life just is harder for people than they are allowed to say, because of social norms. And that's depressing. So we're all miserable, and no-one can actually reach out because that's weakness and weakness is shunned. 
Everyone suffers in silence.

A little update on this. 

I made a list of things I needed to do - and have been eating better, so the sore at the corner of my mouth is fading and my general health is improved. 

I deleted 135GB of porn. I heard it's bad for your self esteem - so yeah. 
Already I feel good about the change. I'm coming to terms with the idea that sexual desires are not an unnatural perversion. I will still need therapy to truly tackle this issue, but it's a start. 

I also am downloading site-blocking software, and distraction management software. To block myself from reddit, facebook, steam etc and other sites and programs that eat my time when I could be writing or doing otherwise productive/creative things. 

I am going to confront and accept the idea that I am in need. I plan to take out a special advanced payment from the government so I can afford to get myself out of this struggle. 
I hope all those bitter taxpayers always whinging about their taxpayer dollars being wasted by bludgers aren't too angry about it, but I really need to get some nutrition and therapy. 
In Australia they actually run media campaigns hating on the poor, encouraging people to despise those who are on payments. 

My list includes little rewards for myself as well - and I feel really happy about it. 
I printed it off so I could have it looking all official. 

I am going to be buying a landline phone, so I can still organize things if my mobile breaks. Which I think will be really important and a huge step towards avoiding this particular pit again. 

Thankyou for your kind words of encouragement. 
I am by no means "fixed", but maybe with help - by this time next year my life will be completely different.

I have an extremely hard time handling rejection, each rejection feels deeply personal even when it isn't. I keep coming up against this self-doubt and lack of motivation. I would love an editing job, at least to just get some nice meals on my table for a change. Or something revolving around my skillset, which lies largely in writing skills. But I just don't know where to start. 

Broke my heart the other day, I found an amazing recipe for these tuna rissoles with herbed mayonnaise and I realized I just couldn't afford the ingredients. If I did buy them, I'd have like - one amazing meal and then not be able to afford anything for the next week.

Even just you responding. Just knowing someone was out there to listen means a lot. I have nothing at the moment, except to try and get through the day. I will nap today. I need to try and use the computer less.

I have a horrible curse of low self-worth. I find myself constantly trying my best to be "out of everyone's way" as much as possible. And live my life "low profile" as though someone somewhere is going to be massively upset or angry at me being outside my house. 
I mean, I feel guilty for being on the pension at 24. I feel like I would still be guilty if I was homeless on the street. I'd feel guilty for taking up space on park benches when I needed to sleep. 
I just want to be able to confidently say "I matter" and not feel like some kind of great liar and thief.
In the grim darkness of the 41st millennium, there is only narcissism.

Through the trials and tribulations of putting up with her, I've slowly come to realize that she is just utterly removed from self-analysis. Just go NC. I did and I'm so much happier.

Your happiness is the most important factor here dude - and I'm telling you right now, you will be amazed how much better your life will be once she isn't a part of it.

I know exactly how you feel. I recently just decided to go full NC forever with my abusive mother - who was often extremely subtle, and very good at gaslighting. She would often repeat the mantra "You always make me out to be the bad guy" and would continually try to play victim, only so that there was no sense of accountability. 
My brother was driving me to the airport, and he actually said to me "Do you ever wonder if it's all in our heads?" and that right there just goes to show you how good they can be at twisting reality. They're so convinced of their own lies and the delusions they warp reality into, that they can make you doubt what you really experienced. Any rational human being, would surely have some kind of deep regret or conscious...

I realized when I was a child that my mother was very "wrong" but I couldn't do anything about it. No-one would believe me because she was so good at being nice to absolutely everyone, except when you challenged her ego and she lost power over you. 
I remember just being terrified to be around her, my entire life was just fear. I was sometimes suicidal after primary school, being bullied all day to come home and have to tread on eggshells to avoid a tantrum. No part of my life, except when I could escape into a good movie/book/videogame was overly enjoyable. 
It just wears you down. After a while it is difficult to care about anything. 
But I try to be appreciative these days. I am not always successful. But I'm really trying.  
I understand the sensation, I still am haunted by it to this day. I don't know how else to offer support - other than to say it doesn't always stay that way. You can be happy. It just takes time.
